name: Atrophic Lichen Planus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Lichen Planus

criteria.description: Presence of atrophic, violaceous, polygonal papules or plaques with characteristic Wickham striae
Histological features showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermoepidermal junction with basal cell degeneration and epidermal atrophy
Positive direct immunofluorescence showing fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane zone

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation consistent with atrophic lichen planus plus confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from other lichenoid dermatoses is essential; biopsy is recommended.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Atrophic violaceous polygonal papules and plaques
Wickham striae (fine white reticulated lines on lesions)
searchTerms: fine white lines on skin lesions

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Epidermal atrophy with shiny, thin skin
searchTerms: thin shiny skin with epidermal thinning
loss of skin thickness with shine

common.symptomName: Lesions predominantly on extremities and trunk
searchTerms: skin lesions mainly on arms, legs, and torso
rash mostly on limbs and trunk
spots appearing on extremities and body

occasional.symptomName: Oral mucosal involvement with white reticular plaques
searchTerms: reticular white plaques on oral mucosa

occasional.symptomName: Nail dystrophy including longitudinal ridging and thinning
searchTerms: nail changes with ridges and thinning
nail dystrophy with grooves and fragility

occasional.symptomName: Mild localized pain or burning sensation
searchTerms: mild localized skin pain or burning
low level burning or aching in skin
skin reaction similar to lichen planus from drugs

laboratory: Histopathology showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at dermoepidermal junction
Direct immunofluorescence positive for fibrinogen along basement membrane
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic papules and plaques with Wickham striae

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of porcelain-white atrophic plaques with follicular plugging
Histopathology shows homogenization of collagen in upper dermis
Thickened, lichenified plaques due to chronic scratching
Absence of Wickham striae and band-like lymphocytic infiltrate

redFlags: Rapid progression of atrophic lesions with ulceration
Development of squamous cell carcinoma within chronic lesions
Severe pain or bleeding from lesions
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Wickham ER. Clinical and histopathological features of lichen planus variants. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018.
